The metaphors deepen both the immediate experience and the story’s themes: the congregation becomes “a single animal” during its panic, while Barbara imagines her pregnant body as “a kind of argument no one could answer.” The recurring three steps toward the shooter turn physical distance into a measure of her faith in human connection—and its devastating limits. Colloquial idiom such as “Nobody would say boo” also lends authenticity to the dialogue.
